Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts

Ledger has confirmed that some of its devices distributed through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis were compromised with a hardware implant that drained users' cryptocurrency wallets.

The company has been investigating reports of users losing funds from wallets purchased through CryptoBilis, a major Malaysia-based hardware wallet retailer operating across Southeast Asia.

Some researchers have shown the implant in Ledger X since September 16, saying tampered devices were available for nearly half the price of the original hardware.

Ledger wallets are physical devices designed to securely store the private keys that control cryptocurrency assets and authorize transactions.

On October 9, Ledger said it had launched an investigation into user reports of cryptocurrency losses and asked CryptoBilis to stop selling and shipping Ledger devices.

The next day, the company confirmed hardware tampering on at least one device, though it’s still unclear exactly how or when the devices were tampered with.

"Ledger can confirm that one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger is reaching out to impacted users as part of the ongoing investigation," Ledger said.

The crypto wallet maker also noted that it was working with authorities to identify the perpetrator and bring them to justice.

“[...]Ledger recommends users who purchased a Ledger device from this reseller to not initiate set up if they have not yet done so. If you have set up your Ledger device, consider moving assets to a new Ledger signer (with a new seed),” warned Ledger .

Yesterday, Ledger provided another update , confirming that all user reports of unexpected fund drains were linked to devices sold through CryptoBilis and describing the affected volume as “limited.”

While the company did not disclose the type of devices compromised in this supply-chain attack, reports online talk about a spy implant in Ledger X devices that blends with the legitimate hardware.

Mark Karpelès, currently leading Karpeles Lab Inc. and CTO at Shells.com, showed a picture of the new implant in Ledger X, saying that it was "quite an evolution" from previous versions featuring manually soldered wires.

The former CEO of Mt. Gox said the implant was concealed behind the screen, but its antenna cable would have indicated that something was wrong.

According to Karpelès, the malicious hardware captured the device's display output and button presses to identify the seed phrase, then transmitted it to the attacker over an LTE connection using an eSIM.

"Ledger Nano X are used to store crypto. The spy implants are used to steal whatever crypto you store in those Ledger Nano X," Karpelès explained .

Although the CEO did not name CryptoBilis as the vendor of the compromised LedgerX, he said the device was not purchased via Ledger's recommended channels but from "a well known platform via a Chinese seller (product shipped from Malaysia)."

Tibane Labs, a cryptocurrency research and development studio, confirmed Karpelès' finding, adding that there were two implant versions for Ledger X.

The researchers obtained two variants, one in a Ledger device bought on Amazon Japan from " China-based seller · shipped from Malaysia," the other purchased on Yahoo! Auctions, Japan.

In a report over the weekend, Tibane Labs notes that the threat actor made room for the malicious circuitry by replacing the original battery with a smaller one, which powers both the implant and the Ledger X.

"Under the battery and antenna sits an ST STM32G431KBU6 (Arm Cortex‑M4, 128 KB flash, UFQFPN‑32)," the researchers found inside one of the devices.

For connectivity, the actor used "a tiny eSIM, an 8‑pad package just 2×2 mm, next to the MCU, and a shielded LTE module that sends the words out."

items.title: Palantir's Europe head warns the region is 'missing the boat' on AI just as it did with the internet
items.content:
Palantir (PLTR) head of U.K. and Europe Louis Mosley warned that the region is making the same mistake with artificial intelligence (AI) that it made with the internet.

Where the U.S. "got the internet right," built a score of businesses and became the backbone of the digital economy, Europe "missed the boat," Mosley told CoinDesk in an interview.

The divergence between the markets in the decades since has been stark. Europe and the U.S. were roughly comparable 20 years ago on GDP per capita, capital-market depth and the scale of their largest companies. Since then, t he U.S. has compounded growth while Europe has barely advanced in comparison.

Previous technology waves produced European champions. The internet wave produced almost none, with ASML (ASML) the rare exception, he said.

“It’s by far and away the largest European company . Which is, it tells you that the value is in tech,” he said.

Mosley, Palantir's executive vice president for the U.K and Europe, argued AI will be even more consequential. European corporates remain cautious, with an attitude of “This is new, that means it could be risky. I’ll wait and see,” according to Mosley.

Palantir builds an ontology and governance scaffold that lets governments and companies deploy large language models and agents in healthcare, industry or defense.

Mosley called the company “the purest proxy on public markets for the rate of AI adoption in an economy.” Palantir is model-agnostic: customers can run OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, open-weight models or Chinese systems and fine-tune them on their own data.

Opposition to Palantir across the U.K. and Europe stems from its deep defense and law enforcement ties, including providing surveillance software to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) under the administration of President Donald Trump and supplying targeting systems to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF). Campaigners have argued against the use of Palantir in systems used by the public services such as the U.K.'s National Health Service (NHS) on ethical grounds.

“The issues that really get those people fired up are Gaza and Trump," Mosley told CoinDesk. "Palantir has contracts in America for Trump’s administration and has contracts in Israel with the IDF and we have a contract with the NHS.”

Mosley called this a distraction from domestic priorities, asking whether politicians would tell a constituent they must wait longer for a hip operation because of a supplier’s unrelated foreign contracts.

Political hostility to energy-intensive tech is commonplace: bitcoin miners were attacked over electricity use a decade ago. Many of them have now pivoted to AI high-performance computing and face identical criticism over power consumption.

While it’s true AI will disrupt jobs, it will also free nurses and police from paperwork, raising productivity, he said. With only around 1,000 customers against a far larger addressable market of complex organizations in allied countries, Mosley said he still sees Palantir as early.

The biggest risk to AI, he said, remains political failure to explain why the technology is good for people.

“You’re making all the same mistakes again,” Mosley noted of the recurring political response. “In the end, I want to believe that good wins out over bad.”

items.title: Clearing chat history helps AI agents find better solutions
items.summary: Microsoft researchers found that autonomous AI agents get trapped in what they call "idea basins" because of their growing chat context, local solution regions they can't escape. Their "Fork-and-Flush" method clears the chat history but keeps the workspace, achieving up to 66 per
items.content:
Clearing chat history helps AI agents find better solutions

View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian

Long-running AI research agents can plateau despite additional compute, a Microsoft Research study finds. Accumulated conversation context can constrain their search, keeping them focused on similar solutions instead of exploring better approaches.

Microsoft researchers studied what they call "Autoresearch agents," AI systems that repeatedly propose solutions, evaluate them, and refine them based on feedback. Eight independent runs of the same agent on the same task plateaued at significantly different performance levels, with final scores ranging from 68.3 to 100.0. These gaps persisted even with substantially more compute, according to the paper.

The researchers plotted solutions from all runs on a two-dimensional map that places similar solutions close together, then compared them. Solutions from a single run almost always stayed within a small region of the map. The authors call these regions "idea basins."

The agents spend a large share of their remaining compute budget refining solutions within a less productive region instead of finding better approaches discovered by other runs. This pattern persists even when the agents periodically compress their conversation histories.

Clearing chat history lets agents explore new approaches

The proposed method, "Fork-and-Flush," combines two mechanisms. In "forking," the agent splits into K parallel branches, each inheriting the previous workspace and all generated files. In "flushing," each branch loses its entire chat context but keeps the workspace, allowing it to start a fresh conversation and build on prior work.

On the left, a single run (gray, dashed) keeps refining solutions within the same idea basin. Fork-and-Flush starts parallel branches with fresh chat contexts, keeps the best branch, and discards the rest. On the right, a branch with fresh context moves into a different idea basin and achieves a higher score. | Image: Cai, Ziakas et al. (2026)

A branch that keeps the parent process's chat context tends to return to the same idea basin because the previous reasoning steers its next steps. Fresh context restores diversity in the search. The conversation history is lost, but the code, files, and saved results remain in the workspace.

A 66 percent higher normalized average score on the same compute budget

The researchers tested Fork-and-Flush on 13 long-running tasks , including polyomino packing, job-shop scheduling, and cryptanalysis. The tasks also included compressing a CIFAR classifier and optimizing a VLIW kernel. Individual runs lasted from several hours to over 100 hours. The agents used GPT-5.6-terra and GPT-5.5 through the GitHub Copilot CLI.

On the same compute budget, Fork-and-Flush achieved a min-max-normalized average score of 0.78, compared to 0.47 for single runs and 0.54 for best-of-4. The paper reports relative gains of 66.0 and 44.4 percent, respectively. The method achieved the highest mean score on 12 of the 13 tasks.

Fork-and-Flush also produced more consistent results, with normalized standard deviation falling to 0.16 from 0.26 for single runs. Simply clearing the chat context without branching improved results by 22 percent.

Relative improvement over the respective single-run baseline

Stronger models may still need context resets

The researchers also tested whether more capable models avoid idea basins, using MAX-3-SAT problems across three model sizes, Qwen3.5-4B, 9B, and 27B. Variance between runs followed an inverted U-shaped curve, peaking on tasks at the edge of a model's abilities, roughly halfway between random-guessing performance and the reference solver's performance.

Results vary most on tasks at the edge of a model's abilities, with some runs succeeding and others falling well short. Models almost always succeed on very easy tasks and fail on very hard ones. This pattern holds across all three model sizes tested.…

items.content:
음성 AI가 차세대 인터페이스로 주목받으며 관련 스타트업에 대규모 투자가 이어지고 있지만, 아직 대중적인 전환점을 맞이하지는 못했다는 진단이 나왔다. 대화 속도와 음성 인식 정확도, 감정 표현, 사용자 신뢰 등 해결해야 할 과제가 남아 있다는 분석이다.

테크크런치에 따르면, 기업용 음성 AI 플랫폼 폴리AI(PolyAI)의 숀 웬 최고 기술책임자(CTO)와 회의록 작성 전문 오터(Otter)의 알렉스 게이 최고 마케팅책임자(CMO)는 최근 열린 '휴먼X' 컨퍼런스에서 음성 AI 기술의 발전과 한계를 짚었다.

웬 CTO는 "음성 AI는 아직 확실한 '챗GPT 모멘트'를 맞이하지 못했다"고 평가했다. 그는 "듣기와 말하기가 동시에 아뤄지는 전이중 모델(Full-duplex)을 개발하는 이정표에는 도달했지만, 다음 과제는 모델이 답을 빠르게 찾아 대화가 자연스럽게 느껴지도록 추론 속도를 높이는 것"이라고 분석했다.

음성 AI가 사람처럼 말하는 것만으로는 충분하지 않다는 지적도 나왔다. 특히 고객 상담 분야에서는 AI가 기계적인 말투를 벗어나 실제 문제를 해결할 수 있다는 확신을 줘야 한다는 설명이다.

웬 CTO는 고객이 처음 두세 차례 대화에서 AI 상담원과 소통할 의향을 보이고, 이후 문제 해결 능력을 확인하면 신뢰가 쌓일 수 있다고 봤다. AI가 충분한 성능을 보여준다면 고객이 굳이 사람 상담원과 통화할 필요가 없다고 느끼게 된다는 것이다.

게이 CMO는 기업 업무 자동화를 위해 발화자 식별과 사용자 의도 파악, 조직 내부 지식의 체계화가 중요하다고 설명했다. 회의 내용을 기록하는 데서 나아가 실제 업무를 수행하려면 누가 어떤 의도로 발언했는지 이해하고, 이를 기업의 전문 지식과 연결해야 한다는 의미다.

감정 표현도 중요한 과제로 꼽았다. 오터는 회의에서 특정 인물을 대신할 수 있는 디지털 트윈 기술을 개발하고 있다. 그러나 AI 아바타가 사람과 대화할 때의 감정적 표현을 충분히 전달하지 못하면 토론이나 전략적 논의를 이끌기 어렵다고 지적했다.

그는 회의에서 의미 있는 대화는 단순한 질문과 답변을 넘어 토론과 전략적 논의, 참여자 사이의 관계를 바탕으로 이뤄진다며, 이런 요소가 빠지면 AI 아바타는 결국 질의응답형 챗봇에 머물 수 있다고 말했다.

음성 인식 정확도도 해결해야 할 문제로 꼽혔다. 웬 CTO는 자동 음성 인식(ASR) 모델이 중요한 키워드를 놓치면 대화 전체의 맥락을 파악하기 어려워진다고 설명했다. 회의록 작성 서비스에서 잘못된 전사 결과는 요약과 후속 업무 처리까지 연쇄적으로 오류를 일으킬 수 있다.

게이 CMO는 "전사는 오터가 궁극적으로 추구하는 목표가 아니라 생산성을 높이기 위한 출발점"이라며 "초기 전사 결과가 정확하지 않으면 이후의 모든 작업이 잘못될 수 있다"고 말했다. 잘못된 결과를 바탕으로 실제 업무까지 처리하면 플랫폼에 대한 신뢰가 무너질 수 있는 만큼, 음성 인식 모델을 지속적으로 개선해야 한다는 설명이다.

AI 음성 도구를 사용할 때 투명성을 확보하는 일도 중요하다. 기업 통화나 회의에서 상대방이 AI와 대화하고 있는지, 발언이 녹음되고 있는지를 명확하게 알려야 한다는 것이다.

오터는 회의에 AI 봇이 직접 참여하지 않는 때에도 채팅 등을 통해 녹음 사실을 알리는 방안을 고려하고 있다. 폴리AI도 기업 통화에서 고객이 AI와 대화하고 있다는 사실을 분명히 밝히는 것이 신뢰 형성에 필수적이라고 강조했다.

items.content:
Cyberattack shuts down refrigerators at French supermarkets

Attackers remotely defrosted refrigerators at multiple French supermarket chains overnight in a cyberattack that reportedly targeted Danfoss refrigeration controllers.

Victims include Intermarché, Coopérative U, Carrefour Market, Monoprix, Leclerc, and Super U, with French outlets reporting that the attack affected 250 to 350 stores, causing significant financial losses and food waste.

The threat actors hijacked refrigeration controllers running older versions of Danfoss control software on Sunday night and used them to raise supermarket refrigerator temperatures by triggering a built-in automatic defrosting system.

"Following a cyberattack reportedly affecting a service provider that manages refrigeration systems in stores, some fresh and frozen food display units are out of service," an Intermarché spokesperson told BleepingComputer when asked for more information on the incident. "Intermarché and Netto have taken all necessary precautions to remove the products from these units as quickly as possible. We don't have further information currently, nor a specific list of affected stores to share with you."

Coopérative U president Dominique Schelcher also confirmed the incident earlier today and said that the attack affected multiple stores in the chain.

"I can confirm that, since last night, a cyberattack has been affecting the refrigeration systems in several stores within our @CooperativeU network. Our teams are fully mobilized, working alongside refrigeration specialists, to resolve the situation as quickly as possible. An investigation will be conducted to shed full light on this attack," Schelcher said .

"Targeting equipment essential for preserving fresh produce and supplying food to the French people is an extremely serious matter and is unprecedented. It is unacceptable."

Cold chain breakage warning sign in French supermarket ( Alejo Schapire )

EU agriculture and food commissioner Christophe Hansen also condemned the attack and named France's largest supermarket chain, Leclerc, as one of the victims.

The Paris prosecutor's office has told AFP that it has opened an investigation into "the large-scale cyberattack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France" to "identify the victims and establish the link with the damage they reported in terms of foodstuff losses and the outbreak of fires."

While no information is available on how the Danfoss refrigeration controllers were compromised, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned  in May 2025 of an authentication bypass vulnerability ( CVE-2025-41450 ) and in August 2025 of a command injection flaw ( CVE-2025-41451 ) in the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series hardware platform used to manage refrigeration and HVAC systems typically found in the food retail sector.

Claroty's Team82 research team, which found the two flaws, also published a detailed write-up  in August on how they can be exploited to achieve remote code execution on Danfoss AK-SM 800A publicly accessible management interfaces.

While researching the attack surface, Predicta Lab CEO Baptiste Robert found 2752 Danfoss systems  exposed online on Monday, 1590 of them in France. Shodan, a search engine for Internet-connected devices, is also tracking over 4,500 Danfoss devices reachable over the Internet.

Internet-exposed Danfoss systems (Baptiste Robert)

Spokespersons for Danfoss, Leclerc, and Coopérative U were not immediately available for comment when contacted by BleepingComputer earlier today.

Although there is no evidence yet that the two are connected, retail giant Ahold Delhaize, one of the world's largest food retail chains, also announced on Monday that it had to take some systems offline after a "cybersecurity incident."

Update October 12, 13:23 EDT: Added Intermarché statement and more info on Danfoss systems exposed online.

items.content:
Some meetings last longer than it took attackers to jump on a newly disclosed security flaw this week. Within hours, they were already testing it. That's not much time to read the warning, let alone do something about it.

But speed is only part of the problem. A secure connection didn't always mean a safe destination. People offering to fix a ransomware mess had questions to answer themselves. Malware got better at hiding its tracks. And some systems turned out to be easier to break into than anyone would like to admit. The odd part is how normal much of it looked until someone checked closer.

There's more going on here than a few bad bugs and clever attacks. Some of the smaller stories are just as telling. This week's full recap is worth a read, especially the bits that didn't make the big headlines.

Atlassian Flaw Exploited in the Wild — Threat actors have begun to exploit a newly disclosed critical security flaw impacting Atlassian Data Center products that could allow access to sensitive files under certain conditions. The arbitrary file access flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-21589 (CVSS score: 9.3) affects multiple products, including Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center, Crowd Data Center, Crucible, and Fisheye. The exploitation activity targeting its honeypot network is said to have begun two hours after watchTowr released additional technical details of the vulnerability.

Replace legacy DB tools with a modern platform that connects to every major database from one interface and eliminates locally stored credentials. Available for download as a free desktop app or as part of KeeperPAM.

Bugs drop weekly, and the gap between a patch and an exploit is shrinking fast. These are the heavy hitters for the week: high-severity, widely used, or already being poked at in the wild.

Check the list, patch what you have, and hit the ones marked urgent first — CVE-2026-86360, CVE-2026-86361, CVE-2026-86362 (Dell System Update), CVE-2026-21589 (Atlassian), CVE-2026-93355 (LiteLLM), CVE-2026-106382, CVE-2026-106197, CVE-2026-106358, CVE-2026-106347 (Google Chrome), CVE-2026-102255 (SonicWall SMA 1000), CVE-2026-105192 (LMCache), CVE-2026-102406, CVE-2026-103008, CVE-2026-102404, CVE-2026-102413 (Elasticsearch), CVE-2026-104711, CVE-2026-104712, CVE-2026-104713, CVE-2026-104714 (Apache Struts), CVE-2026-91140 (Progress DataDirect), CVE-2025-64393, CVE-2026-58069 (Veeam Backup & Replication), CVE-2026-32740 (Next.js), CVE-2026-18397 (Thales SConnect), CVE-2026-84388 ( Fortinet FortiPAM Chrome extension ), CVE-2026-76464, CVE-2026-20328, CVE-2026-76454, CVEs, CVE-2026-76482, CVE-2026-76480, CVE-2026-76483, CVE-2026-76455, CVE-2026-76459, CVE-2026-76471, CVE-2026-76465, CVE-2026-76485, CVE-2026-76486, CVE-2026-76501, CVE-2026-76498, CVE-2026-76499, CVE-2026-76500 ( Cisco ), CVE-2026-76281, CVE-2026-76282, CVE-2026-76284 , CVE-2026-76268 (Splunk), CVE-2026-85097 (Bricksforge WordPress plugin), CVE-2026-93836 (WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce WordPress plugin), CVE-2026-94504 (Ninja Forms WordPress plugin), CVE-2026-105133, CVE-2026-105134 (AhsayCBS), CVE-2026-96940 (Microsoft Exchange Server), CVE-2026-63277 (LibreOffice), CVE-2026-59265 (Apache OpenOffice), and multiple vulnerabilities in WordPress.

A few arrests and takedowns brought some good news this week. But the bigger picture is less comforting. Attackers keep finding new ways in, old mistakes still work, and even the systems meant to help or protect people aren't always what they seem.

That's it for this edition. Not every story here needs your attention, but a few might deserve a closer look. Especially the ones that sound a little too familiar to your own setup. Better to spot the problem in someone else's story than become part of the next one. See you next week.

items.content:
CSC가 '제10회 사이버시큐리티 브레이크스루 어워즈(CyberSecurity Breakthrough Awards)'에서 '위협 인텔리전스 혁신(Threat Intelligence Innovation)' 부문을 수상했다고 12일 밝혔다.

이번에 수상한 '3D 도메인 보안 및 글로벌 집행(3D Domain Security and Global Enforcement)' 솔루션은 첨단 AI 머신러닝 기술과 도메인 위협 인텔리전스, 통합 글로벌 집행 기능을 결합한 플랫폼이다. 조직은 이를 통해 소셜미디어, 검색엔진, 이메일, 전자상거래 웹사이트 등에서 자사 브랜드를 겨냥한 외부 사이버 위협을 탐지하고 대응할 수 있다.

이 솔루션은 방화벽 외부 및 기업 경계 밖의 위협 벡터를 다차원적으로 파악하도록 돕는다. 관련 위협 벡터 탐지 건수를 평균 23% 늘리고, 사이버 범죄자가 악용하기 전에 휴면 도메인 같은 사각지대를 드러내는 역할을 한다.

기반이 되는 '도메인섹(DomainSec)' 플랫폼은 외부 인텔리전스를 활용해 제로 트러스트(Zero Trust) 전략을 지원한다. 특히 도메인섹 위험 점수(DomainSec risk score) 모델을 통해 위험도가 높은 도메인을 식별하고 우선순위를 지정할 수 있어 대기업이 자원을 효율적으로 관리하도록 돕는다.

이합 슈라임(Ihab Shraim) CSC 디지털 브랜드 서비스 부문 최고기술책임자는 "도메인 기반 위협은 피싱 캠페인, 브랜드 사칭, 악성코드 배포의 중심에 있다"며 "이번 수상은 고객이 진화하는 사이버 위협으로부터 온라인 입지를 안전하게 보호할 수 있도록 지원하겠다는 약속을 보여준다"고 말했다.

items.title: IonQ to Acquire Zero Trust Firm Elisity for Up to $1.3 Billion
items.summary: The all-stock deal brings Elisity’s least-privilege access technology into IonQ’s security portfolio. The post IonQ to Acquire Zero Trust Firm Elisity for Up to $1.3 Billion appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
IonQ on Monday said it signed a definitive agreement to buy Elisity in a stock-only transaction worth up to $1.3 billion.

Up to $150 million of that amount is earnout consideration, contingent on how Elisity’s business performs. IonQ expects to complete the acquisition in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The number of IonQ shares issued will depend on the company’s volume-weighted average price over 20 trading days ending shortly before closing, but the price will be kept between $33.07 and $49.61.

Founded in 2019, Elisity sells software that restricts which users, devices, workloads and AI agents can communicate on enterprise networks, based on least-privilege policies. A component called IdentityGraph combines what Elisity collects itself with data from partner tools, including identity, asset and risk details, to guide access decisions.

According to IonQ, Elisity has more than 100 customer deployments. The startup raised more than $70 million.

IonQ’s portfolio spans quantum computing, networking, sensing and security, and the company already offers post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and quantum key distribution (QKD). It plans to use Elisity’s customer and CISO relationships to reach more enterprise and government buyers for those technologies and its quantum computing products. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

The two companies plan to add cryptographic inventory and risk data to IdentityGraph. The goal is to help organizations decide which post-quantum upgrades to tackle first, weighing business risk and the criticality of affected operations.

“Access controls reduce exposure; cryptographic upgrades would address the underlying weaknesses,” Elisity CEO James Winebrenner wrote in a blog post on the deal. In a press release, he noted: “Our customers need to prioritize post-quantum cryptography initiatives while securing existing assets to keep essential operations running.”

IonQ CEO Niccolo de Masi pointed to Q-Day, the point at which quantum computers could break widely used public-key encryption. “Q-Day is coming much faster than predicted,” he said. IonQ also cited recent White House executive orders promoting quantum technology and pushing federal agencies to adopt PQC sooner.

Once the deal is completed, Winebrenner and Elisity’s existing management team will remain in charge of the business.
